PART 2 TEST METHODS

1

Scope
to the species

This parl of ISO 5565 specifies test methods for the analysis of vanilla belonging (Salisbury) Ames, syn. Vanilla p/anifo/ia Andrews.
This part of ISO 5565 is applicable vanilla extracts.

Vanilla fragrar?s

to vanilla in pods, cut in bulk, and in the form of powder. It is not applicable

to

Three test methods for the analysis of vanilla are described in this part of ISO 5565: a) b) the determination of moisture content in vanilla pods and powder (4.1); 4-hydroxybenzaldehyde and 4-hydroxybenzoic acid by high-

the determination of vanillin, vanillic acid, performance liquid chromatography (4.2); the determination

c)

of vanillin content by an ultraviolet spectrometric

method (4.3).

NOTE

Specifications for vanilla are given in ISO 5565-1.

4 4.1

Test methods Determination of moisture content in vanilla pods and powder

NOTE 4.1.1

The general method described in ISO 939 is not applicable to vanilla,

Principle
is determined using a water-immiscible organic liquid. The

The amount of water entrained by azeotropic distillation water is collected in a graduated tube. 4.1.2

Reagent
water or water of equivalent purity.

Use only reagents of recognized analytical grade, and distilled or demineralized 4.1.2.1

Toluene

Saturate the toluene by shaking it with a small quantity of water and distil it. Use the distillate for the determination of the moisture. 4.1.3 Apparatus apparatus and, in particular, the following. means and provided with a

Usual laboratory

4.1.3.1 Dktillation apparatus, consisting of a glass flask heated by a suitable reflux condenser discharging into a receiver connected to the flask.

The connections between the receiver, the condenser and the flask are interchangeable ground glass joints. The receiver serves to collect and measure the condensed water, and to return the solvent to the flask. The assembly of the apparatus is shown in Figure 1 and the various components are described below. 4.1.3.1.1 annealed Flask, of capacity 500 ml, of the shape shown in Figure 1 and made of heat-resistant and as free as possible from striae and similar defects. glass, well

Reflux condenser, water cooled, made of glass, having a jacket approximately 4.1.3.1.2 inner tube of diameter 9,5 mm to 12,5 mm.

400 mm long and an

The tip of the condenser to be inserted in the receiver maybe ground off at an angle of 30� from the vertical axis of the condenser. When inserted into the receiver, the tip of the condenser shall be 6 mm to 7 mm above the surface of the liquid in the receiver after distillation conditions have been established. 4.1.3.1.3 Receiver, of capacity 5 ml, made of heat-resistant glass, well annealed and as free as possible from striae and similar defects, provided with ground glass joints, with the shape, dimensions and tolerances given in Figure 1. It consists essentially of an upper chamber, together with a tube and ground joint leading to a flask and graduated tube. The graduated portion shall have a capacity of 5 ml when filled to the highest graduation mark. The scale shall cover the range of O ml to 5 ml and shall be graduated at intervals of 0,10 ml. The graduation corresponding to each millilitre shall be numbered and carried completely round the tube. The graduation midway between the numbered marks shall be carried three-quarters of the way round, and the remaining shall be carried half-way round the tube. The error at any indicated capacity shall not exceed 0,05 ml. 4.1.3.1.4 -Heat source, of heat control. either an oil bath or an electric marks marks marks

heater, provided with a sliding rheostat or other means

4.1.5 4.1.5.1

Procedure
Preparation of apparatus

Clean the entire apparatus with a potassium dichromateMfuric acid cleaning solution to minimize the adherence of water droplets to the sides of the condenser and the receiver. Rinse thoroughly with water and dry completely before use.

4.1.5.2

Test portion

Weigh, to the nearest 0,1 g, about 10 g of the test sample (4.1.4) such that the quantity of water collected will not exceed 4,5 ml. 4.1.5.3 Determination

Transfer quantitatively the test portion (4.1 .5.2) to the distillation flask (4.1.3.1.1) using toluene (4.1 .2.1). Add sufficient toluene (about 75 ml in all) to cover the sample completely and swirl to mix. Assemble the apparatus and fill the receiver (4.1 .3.1 .3) with the toluene by pouring it through the condenser (4.1 ,3.1.2) until it begins to overflow into the distillation flask. If necessary, insert a loose cotton plug in the top of the condenser or attach to it a small calcium chloride tube to prevent condensation of atmospheric moisture within the condenser tube. In order to control refluxing, wrap the flask and tube so that the distillation rate is about 100 drops per increase the distillation rate to about 200 drops per reflux condenser occasionally during the distillation adhering to the walls of the condenser. The water and down the water condenser leading to the receiver with a cloth minute. When the greater parl of minute and continue until no more with 5 ml portions of the toluene for insulation. Heat the flask the water has distilled over, water is collected. Purge the to wash down any moisture

in the receiver maybe made to separate from the toluene by occasionally moving a spiral copper wire up in the condenser and receiver, thus causing the water to settle at the bottom of the receiver. Reflux until level in the receiver remains unchanged for 30 min and then shut off the source of heat. Flush the with toluene as required, making use of the spiral copper wire to discharge any moisture droplets. for at least 15 min or until the toluene layer is clear; then read

Immerse the receiver in water at room temperature the volume of water. 4.1.6 Expression of results

Preparation

of standard solutions

In the weighing bottle (4.3.3.8) weigh, to the nearest 0,001 g, about 30 mg of the vanillin (4.3.2.3) which has been previously dried in the desiccator (4.3.3.4). Dissolve it in about 20 ml of the ethanol (4.3.2.1) and transfer it quantitatively to a 250 ml volumetric flask (4.3.3.2). Rinse-the weighing bottle several times with the ethanol and pour the washings into the volumetric flask. Dilute to the mark with the ethanol and mix well (solution Al). Pipette 25 ml of solution Al into a 100 ml volumetric flask (4.3.3.2). Dilute to the mark with the ethanol and mix well (solution B1 ). Pipette 10 ml of solution B1 into a 100 ml volumetric flask. Add about 60 ml of the ethanol and 2 ml of the sodium hydroxide solution (4.3.2.2). Mix well. Dilute to the mark with the ethanol and mix well (solution Cl). 4.3.4.1.2 Preparation of reference solution solution (4.3.2.2) into a 100 ml volumetric

Prepare a reference solution by pipetting 2 ml of the sodium hydroxide flask, and diluting to the mark with the ethanol. Mix well. 4.3,4.1.3 Determination

Record the spectrum of solution Cl relative to that of the reference solution (4.3.4.1 .2) over the wavelength 250 nm to 420 nm, using the spectrometer (4.3.3.6) and the cells (4.3.3 .7).' 4.3.4.1.4 Maximum Calculation absorption occurs at (350 ~ 3) nm and its absorbance should be between 0,2 and 0,8.
